newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik Islamic rebels free 35 government captives.
newsitem.headline: Tajik Islamic rebels free 35 government captives.

text.p: Tajikistan's united Islamic opposition on Tuesday released 35 government interior ministry and security troops captured last year when the rebels seized the mountainous region around the central city of Garm.
A Tajik military source told Reuters the servicemen had been brought to the capital, Dushanbe, from Garm, 200 kilometres (125 miles) to the east.

The conciliatory gesture appears to have followed an accord reached between Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and Islamic opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri in neighbouring Afghanistan last month, the source said.
But other armed oppostion groups controlling areas in the Tavildara region have so far not made similar moves and have not released captives they are believed to be holding.
In December, Rakhmonov and Nuri met in Moscow to sign accords on national reconciliation.
The accords map out the powers and functions of a new national reconciliation commission which aims to end a four-year civil war in the former Soviet republic.
Tens of thousands have been killed and many more displaced in fighting between the government and Islamic rebels, which has been further complicated by seething regional and clan rivalries.
